title: Enforcement of Restrictions on Work Pass Holders Working for More Than One Employer
what_it_is: Enforcement of Restrictions on Work Pass Holders Working for More Than One Employer

sections.label: Work pass holder restrictions
sections.summary: Asks how MOM enforces restrictions on work pass holders working outside the designated employer, annual cases of working for more than one employer, and penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how does the Ministry enforce the restrictions on work pass holders carrying on work outside of the designated employer; (b) over the last five years, what is the annual number of cases of work pass holders found to be working for more than one employer at the same time; and (c) what are the penalties for the employer and employee involved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: It is an offence for the work pass holder to perform work for any other person or business entity.

sections.label: Penalties for illegal employment
sections.summary: Between 2016 and 2020, MOM warned an average of 160 work pass holders yearly, debarring them, with fines or imprisonment for holders and employers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2020, MOM issued at least a warning to an average of 160 work pass holders each year who were found to have engaged in illegal employment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: All of them were debarred from working in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Work pass holders found to be engaged in illegal employment will face a fine of up to $2,000 or imprisonment of up to two years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: MOM will also debar them from working in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Likewise, employers who employ any foreigners without a valid work pass will face a fine of up to $30,000 or imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Their work pass privileges will also be suspended.

sections.label: Educational efforts for foreign workers
sections.summary: MOM educates foreign workers on illegal employment, and the in-principle approval letter states the applicant can only work for the specified employer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Beyond that, part of the work also involves educational efforts to make sure that foreign workers working in Singapore understand what constitutes illegal employment or violation of their work permit kind of conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, first, when we give an in-principle approval to the work pass applicants prior to their departure for Singapore, that letter states quite clearly that the work pass applicant can only work for the specified employer in that letter.
